_comment: Human-labeled calibration set for the grounded judge (#1125 §4). Each item pairs a canned ANSWER with the SME human_verdict. `calibrate` grades each answer with the live judge and reports agreement + per-class precision/recall (the misleading class is the gate). The mix deliberately includes fluent-but-wrong (misleading) answers — the hard case an ungrounded judge misses. expected_facts are verbatim from the corpus _Verified: citations. To score the judge live: python3 scripts/rag_gap_harness.py calibrate --judge ollama.

items.query: what is the exact format of a VIN
expected_facts: A VIN is exactly 17 characters matching ^[A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]{17}$: uppercase letters and digits with I, O, Q excluded.
items.answer: A VIN is exactly 17 characters long. It uses uppercase letters and digits, but the letters I, O, and Q are not allowed. The pattern is ^[A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]{17}$.

items.query: what is the exact format of a VIN
expected_facts: A VIN is exactly 17 characters matching ^[A-HJ-NPR-Z0-9]{17}$: uppercase letters and digits with I, O, Q excluded.
items.answer: A VIN is a 16-character code made up of any letters and numbers, including I, O, and Q.

items.query: which service owns purchase order numbers and what do they look like
expected_facts: Purchase orders are owned by pos-inventory (not pos-order).
A PO number is an 8-character, zero-padded, uppercase base-36 code from a Postgres sequence; there is no PO-/year prefix.
items.answer: Purchase orders are owned by the pos-order service, and PO numbers follow the format PO-2026-00042 with the year embedded.

items.query: what permission is needed to read an invoice
expected_facts: Reading an invoice is gated by invoice:manage; there is no invoice:read permission.
items.answer: You need the invoice:read permission to view an invoice.

items.query: is there a required format for a SKU
expected_facts: The SKU is a client-supplied string with no system-enforced length or regex pattern and no auto-generation.
items.answer: Yes, every SKU is auto-generated by the system as an 8-digit numeric code.

items.query: who can approve a permission change
items.answer: I'm sorry, but I don't have access to information about admin governance approvals.

items.query: how do I look up the status of an order
items.answer: You can look up an order's status through the order service using the order lookup by its identifier; the order guide covers the available views and filters.

items.query: what is the format of a workorder number
expected_facts: A workorder number is WO-YYYY-NNNN with the sequence starting at 1000 (e.g. WO-2026-1001).
items.answer: Workorder numbers use the format WO-YYYY-NNNN, for example WO-2026-1001, with the sequence starting at 1000.

items.query: what is the format of a GL chart-of-accounts code
expected_facts: A GL / chart-of-accounts code matches ^\d{4}(-\d{3})?$: four digits, optionally a dash plus three digits.
items.answer: A GL account code is four digits, optionally followed by a dash and three more digits — for example 1000 or 4000-100.

items.query: what does an invoice number look like
expected_facts: An invoice number is INV-<epochMillis>-<first 8 chars of the invoice UUID>, assigned once at draft creation.
items.answer: I don't have that information available.

items.query: how are core charges handled when a customer returns a rebuildable part
items.answer: The platform creates a Return Request linked to the original invoice, runs the rebuild-core rule set to confirm the part is rebuildable, and a Service Rep credits the core charge back through the core-charge ledger in a five-step workflow.

items.query: what is the policy for processing a customer return and issuing a refund on a paid invoice
items.answer: Returns are processed through the Refund Authorization Center, which requires a manager PIN, automatically reverses the original journal entry, and issues store credit within 24 hours under the standard returns SLA.
